St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
Giving Ourselves to God Through...Living, Loving & Learning
St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School is a proud part of the Bosco Catholic Education Trust
Welcome to our school
Welcome to St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School and thank you for visiting our school website which aims to give you an insight of the school as well as providing up to date information for pupils, parents and the wider community. As a Catholic School we strive towards providing a curriculum and learning environment that ensures every child achieves and makes the most of their talents given to them by God. We seek to create an environment where every member of our community feels safe, loved, valued and respected.
We work in partnership with parents and carers and very much value the contribution they make to school life. St Robert’s also enjoys a close partnership with St John’s Parish in Horsham. Because home, school and parish work together, we are able to provide a happy, caring and effective learning environment where expectations are high.
Our school is part of the national Catholic Education Service and functions in partnership with the Catholic Diocese of Arundel and Brighton and West Sussex Local Authority. No content on this website, including photographs, should be copied by any visitors to the site for use elsewhere.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Bright Starts Breakfast Club
At St Robert Southwell we offer a fantastic inhouse Breakfast Club, run by school staff.
Bright Start Breakfast Club offers parents the opportunity to have an exceptional level of childcare on the school site.
Bright Starts is open between 7.30am and 8.40am each day.
Children are offered a choice of breakfast and there is plenty of time to have a play with a wide range of toys, games and craft activities. In good weather, the children also have use of the playground and field.
Places need to be booked for in advance.
It is possible to book the same day each week throughout the school terms, or alternatively, if you work a shift pattern, you can complete the booking forms.
For after school care, St Robert’s works with our partners at Jack and Jill Childcare.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
Performing Arts at St Robert Southwell
At St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, we believe that the performing arts are a powerful way for children to grow in confidence, creativity and community. From their very first term in Reception through to their final year in Year 6, pupils are offered a wealth of opportunities to perform, create and collaborate, both within school and beyond.
Performance Opportunities
Each year group contributes to the life of the school through high-quality performances and celebrations:
EYFS
Nativity play, introducing children to performing in a supportive and joyful setting.
Years 1 - 2
KS1 Nativity and choir performances.
Years 3 - 4
Christmas concerts and participation in the KS2 choir.
Years 5 - 6
End-of-year production, choir, and opportunities for solo or ensemble performance.
KS2
Liturgical celebrations, assemblies, and performance choir events at local venues.
Children experience every element of theatre and performance, whether it be acting, singing, dancing, public speaking, or working behind the scenes with props, set design, costumes, lighting or sound.
Developing Skills and Confidence
Many of our pupils begin their journey with little or no experience of the performing arts. Through our carefully planned, progressive approach, supported by experienced and creative staff, pupils grow in confidence, uncover hidden talents and develop lifelong skills.
Performance teaches children to:
These are skills that extend far beyond the stage, enriching pupils’ learning across the curriculum and preparing them for success at secondary school and in future life.
Collaborate effectively with others.
Solve problems with creativity and resilience.
Show empathy, tolerance and social awareness.
Communicate with clarity and expression.
Cultural and Enrichment Opportunities
We believe it is important that children not only perform but also experience live theatre. Pupils at St Robert Southwell have enjoyed visits to productions such as:
Every Christmas, we also welcome a travelling pantomime company into school, giving all pupils the chance to experience the magic of theatre first-hand.
Expertise and Partnerships
We are blessed with a talented and dedicated staff team, many of whom bring their own experience in musical theatre, dance, music, art, design and costume-making into school life. Their expertise enriches our curriculum and ensures children receive authentic, high-quality guidance.
At St Robert Southwell, the performing arts are for everyone. They are a celebration of talent, teamwork and joy, rooted in our Catholic ethos and our mission to nurture the God-given potential of every child.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, Horsham
St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School is a thriving, high-achieving and aspirational school community located in Roffey, Horsham. As a single-form entry school, we are proud of the close-knit and caring environment we provide, where every child is known, valued and supported to achieve their very best.
Our Catholic ethos is at the heart of all that we do. We believe that each of us is created in the image of God – unique, special and called to flourish. Rooted in Gospel values, we promote kindness, respect, and responsibility, instilling in our pupils the habits of hard work and integrity that will serve them throughout their lives.
We pursue the highest standards of academic achievement and personal development. Whatever a child’s background or starting point, our aim is that by the end of Year 6 every pupil will be equipped with the knowledge, skills and confidence needed to succeed at secondary school and beyond. We want our children to be curious, resilient, and ambitious learners who take pride in their work and in their school.
High standards of behaviour and conduct underpin our culture. Classrooms are calm and purposeful, with a focus on direct teacher instruction and full engagement in learning. Pupils are expected to follow routines, wear their uniform with pride, and demonstrate a commitment to excellence in all that they do. We promote a no-excuses culture: every child can achieve if they work hard, behave well, and live out our shared values.
St Robert Southwell is more than just a school; it is a community of faith, learning and aspiration. We work closely with families and our parish to ensure that every child feels supported, safe and inspired to give their very best.
We warmly welcome prospective parents to visit us and see our vibrant school in action. We look forward to meeting you and to sharing the exciting journey ahead.
Miss Helen ConnorHeadteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
SEND
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) at St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
St Robert Southwell is an inclusive Catholic school. We believe in equality of opportunity for all children, including those whose needs are defined in the Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities Code of Practice 2014 under the four areas of need:
Communication and Interaction
Cognition and Learning
Social, Emotional and Mental Health
Sensory and/or Physical Needs
Our Commitment
At St Robert Southwell, we are dedicated to providing an excellent education for every child, regardless of their individual needs. Our committed team of teachers and support staff work together to ensure that children with additional needs are supported to make progress and achieve their personal goals.
Special needs provision is coordinated by our SENDCo, who works closely with staff, families, and external agencies to ensure the right support is in place.
We are determined to remove barriers to learning, support pupils to thrive academically, and help them grow into confident, well-rounded individuals who live out our Catholic values of respect, dignity, and compassion.
Admissions and Inclusion
Our admissions criteria are clearly set out and applied fairly. If a child has an Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan, parents may name St Robert Southwell as their first choice of school. The Local Authority will then approach the school on behalf of the family. The Headteacher, in consultation with the Governing Board, carefully considers whether the school can meet the pupil’s specific needs.
As a Catholic community, we are committed to welcoming and serving the needs of all pupils. Our ethos is inclusive, ensuring that every child is valued and supported. We teach children to recognise that what they share with one another far outweighs any differences.
Working in Partnership with Families
We know that parents are the first educators of their children, and we value the vital role they play. We encourage open, honest and regular communication to ensure the best outcomes for each child.
Support for parents includes:
If a child’s needs are complex or significant, we may, in partnership with parents, request an assessment from the Local Authority for an Education, Health and Care (EHCP) Plan. This sets out the child’s needs, outcomes, and the provision required to support them. Additional funding may also be provided to ensure the right level of support is in place.
Regular meetings to discuss progress and needs.
Our School Support
Children with additional needs are supported by:
SEN Information Report and Local Offer
Our SEND Information Report 2024 sets out how we meet the needs of children with SEND at St Robert Southwell.
The West Sussex Local Offer provides clear information about services available for children, young people, and families in our area. It helps families understand what support they can expect and make informed decisions about what is right for their child.
Our Local Offer explains:
At St Robert Southwell, we are proud of our inclusive community. We strive to ensure that every child is known, loved, and supported to flourish academically, socially, and spiritually.
If you wish to find out more information regarding SEND, please refer to our school policies
SEND at St Robert Southwell
St Robert Southwell is committed to providing an appropriate and high quality education to all the children at our school. We believe that all children, including those identified as having special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), have a common entitlement to a broad and balanced academic and social curriculum. This curriculum should be accessible to them, and they should be fully included in all aspects of school life.
At St Robert’s we believe quality first teaching is vital to ensure all children’s needs are met in all areas of learning. We recognise that in some cases, outside agency support and advice is needed and work alongside them to support children in their learning. At every stage we feel it is important to work alongside parents in supporting children’s learning.
Our SENCO is Mrs Chase. You can contact our SEN team via the school office, by phone (01403 252357) or by email (FAO Mrs Chase – office@strobertsouthwell.co.uk).
Please see the links below for more information about SEN in St Robert’s.

pageCache.pageTitle: Enrichment Clubs – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Enrichment Clubs
Enrichment at St Robert Southwell
At St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, we are deeply committed to providing a rich and varied enrichment programme that inspires curiosity, builds character, and nurtures the God-given gifts of every child. We believe that education extends beyond the classroom, and our enrichment opportunities are designed to enhance learning, foster creativity and support pupils’ spiritual, social and personal growth.
Sport and Physical Activity
Our sports provision is broad, inclusive and designed to encourage both enjoyment and excellence. Pupils have the opportunity to take part in:
Clubs are led by dedicated staff and specialist coaches, giving pupils access to high-quality teaching and opportunities to represent the school in tournaments. Participation builds teamwork, resilience and respect—values that reflect our Catholic ethos.
Football, cross-country, and gymnastics
Dance and martial arts
Athletics, team games and inter-school competitions
Creative and Academic Opportunities
Alongside sport, pupils enjoy access to specialist-led art and computing clubs, which extend and challenge their thinking.
Leadership and Responsibility
Leadership is central to our enrichment offer. Pupils take on meaningful roles through:
Through these opportunities, children learn to serve their community, take responsibility and use their gifts for the common good.
Our Ethos
We ask our children to work hard, be kind because we see these qualities embodied in Christ, who is our example and guide. Through the Gospel, children learn that they are unique, special and precious to God. In turn, they are encouraged to treat others with dignity, love and respect, helping to make our school a happy, safe and welcoming family.
As St Peter reminds us:
Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God’s grace in its various forms.
We believe that every child has been blessed with unique talents. Through our enrichment programme, we nurture these gifts so that they may flourish and be used in service to others, now and in the future.
Bright Start Breakfast Club
From September 2024, we will be running our own Bright Start Breakfast Club.
We have a lovely base for childcare and family learning in St Cuthman’s.
Bright Start offers parents the opportunity to have an exceptional level of childcare on the school site, for up to 30 pupils.
Bright Start Breakfast Club is open between 7.30am and 8.40am each day.
Children are offered a choice of breakfast and there is plenty of time to have a play with a wide range of toys and games. In good weather, the children also have use of the KS1 playground and/or Field.
Please use the booking form below to secure your child’s place. Places need to be booked and paid for in advanced as well as provision for on the day bookings should they be needed.
It is possible to book the same day each week through out the school terms, or alternatively, if you work a shift pattern, you can complete the individual term booking forms. If places are not available, you will be advised by email and placed on a waiting list.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Curriculum – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Curriculum
The School Curriculum at St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
At St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, our curriculum is rooted in the Gospel and our mission statement:
God gave Himself to you; give yourself to God.
We believe that every child is a unique gift of God, called to flourish in a community of faith, respect, love, forgiveness and learning. Our curriculum has been carefully designed to be knowledge-rich, broad, ambitious and inclusive, ensuring that all pupils are well-prepared for the challenges of secondary school and for life in modern Britain.
Curriculum Intent
Our aim is to deliver a curriculum that is both academically rigorous and spiritually enriching. Following the 2014 National Curriculum, we provide a strong foundation of subject-specific knowledge while embedding Catholic Social Teaching across all areas of learning.
Religious Education is the core of our Catholic curriculum and receives a minimum of 10% of taught curriculum time. We follow the Religious Education Directory, To Know You More Clearly, supported by the Diocese of Arundel & Brighton’s Day by Day resources.
The principles that shape our curriculum are:
Our curriculum not only delivers the fundamentals of reading, writing, mathematics and science but also nurtures creativity, imagination and compassion. It is designed to instil a love of learning and to equip pupils with the knowledge, skills and values to live out their vocation in faith and service.
Curriculum Implementation
Our curriculum not only delivers the fundamentals of reading, writing, mathematics and science but also nurtures creativity, imagination and compassion. It is designed to instil a love of learning and to equip pupils with the knowledge, skills and values to live out their vocation in faith and service.
Key features of our implementation include:
Through ClassDojo, parents receive weekly updates on what their child is learning, ensuring strong home–school partnership and reinforcing learning beyond the classroom.
Curriculum Impact
We measure the success of our curriculum in three key ways:
Academic outcomes
Pupils meet or exceed national standards, with strong progress across the curriculum.
Knowledge and Understanding
Pupils can recall and apply what they have learned, speak confidently about their subjects, and make connections between areas of study.
Character and Values
Pupils leave St Robert Southwell as confident, respectful, faith-filled individuals who demonstrate compassion, resilience and curiosity.
Our children are proud of their achievements and can articulate their knowledge with clarity. Inspectors, visitors and parents alike recognise the depth of engagement and enthusiasm for learning across the school.
Core Subjects
The Wider Curriculum
Beyond the core, our curriculum is broad, balanced and inspiring:
Accessibility and Inclusion
Our curriculum is designed to be accessible to all pupils, regardless of background, identity or ability. We make appropriate adaptations for children with special educational needs or disabilities, those who are more able or have particular gifts and talents, and pupils for whom English is an additional language.
We are committed to fulfilling our duties under the Equality Act 2010 and to making reasonable adjustments so that every child can access, enjoy and excel in their learning.
Enrichment and Extra-Curricular Opportunities
We believe that education extends beyond the classroom. Trips, residentials, visitors, performances, clubs and competitions enrich pupils’ experiences and broaden their horizons. Events such as science fairs, arts showcase, liturgical celebrations and charity work enable pupils to share their talents and apply their learning in meaningful ways.
A Curriculum for Life
Our curriculum is designed not only to provide academic excellence but to form the whole child. Through daily life at St Robert Southwell, pupils learn to:
We see our curriculum as a living expression of our faith and mission: academically challenging, spiritually enriching, and inclusive for all. By the time pupils leave St Robert Southwell, they are equipped with the knowledge, skills and values to succeed in secondary school and to live full, purposeful lives in service of God and others.
be confident, curious learners;
respect and care for others;
live out Gospel values;
take pride in their achievements;

pageCache.pageTitle: Parent View – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Parent View
Ofsted Parent View
At St Robert Southwell, we greatly value the partnership between home, school and parish. Working together enables us to provide the very best education and care for your children. One of the ways you can support this partnership is by sharing your views of our school through Ofsted’s Parent View.
Parent View uses the same format as our own school parent questionnaire and gives parents the opportunity to provide feedback at any time during the school year, as well as during an Ofsted inspection.
When our school is notified of its next Ofsted inspection, parents will be invited to complete the Parent View online questionnaire to share their opinions directly with inspectors.
How Parent View Works
Why Your Views Matter
Your feedback plays an important role in:
Parent View
We are always keen to get feedback from parents whether it is something you think we are doing really well or an area you believe we could improve. There are lots of opportunities for you to provide us with this feedback.
One way is to visit the OFSTED Parent View website by following this link, searching for St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, and answering a series of questions.
Parent View – March 2023
Parent View (give your views)
Accessibility
If you do not have access to a computer or mobile device at home, you are warmly invited to use our school computers to complete the Parent View questionnaire.
By working collaboratively as parents, staff and parish, we can ensure that St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School continues to thrive.
Thank you for your continued support in helping us to make our school the very best it can be.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE & Sport Premium – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
PE & Sport Premium
PE & Sport Premium at St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
At St Robert Southwell, we believe that sport and physical activity are an essential part of school life. Our aim is for all pupils to leave primary school physically literate and equipped with the knowledge, skills and motivation to enjoy a healthy, active lifestyle and to participate in sport throughout their lives.
The Primary PE and Sport Premium funding provides additional resources to help us achieve this vision. It is used alongside our main curriculum budget to ensure long-term improvements in the quality of PE and sport.
How the Funding Can Be Used
Schools are encouraged to use the funding to:
Our Commitment at St Robert Southwell
We have a clear PE and Sport development plan to ensure high-quality provision and increased opportunities for all pupils. Our key objectives are to:
Like all primary schools, St Robert Southwell receives specific funding to enhance our provision for PE and sport. We use this to pay for a highly experienced and competent specialist PE teacher to work in the school for one day a week.
You can see the government’s requirements for this grant here. You can read more about what we do and the impact of our work in the documents below.
Providing high-quality sports coaching for children.
Offering professional development opportunities for staff.
Measuring Impact
The impact of the PE & Sport Premium at St Robert Southwell is evaluated against the five key indicators:
1. Engagement of all pupils in regular physical activity – kick-starting healthy lifestyles.
2. Raising the profile of PE and sport across the school as a tool for whole school improvement.
3. Increasing staff confidence, knowledge and skills in teaching PE and sport.
4. Broadening the range of sports and activities offered to pupils.
5. Increasing participation in competitive sport.
We are proud of the progress our pupils make in sport and PE, and we remain committed to providing opportunities for every child to flourish physically, socially, and emotionally through sport.
Pupil Premium
Pupil premium funding is allocated to St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School for children who are either currently eligible for free school meals or have been at any point in the last six years. We use this additional funding in a number of ways, including 1-1 support, emotional support and financial assistance with residential trips, outings and clubs.
Please use the following links if you would like more details about pupil premium, or information to see if your child could be eligible for pupil premium funding. We would encourage any parent or carer who thinks their child may be eligible for pupil premium funding to contact the school office. All discussions will be entirely confidential.
You can see details of how we spent our pupil premium funding throughout the years and its impact by viewing the table below.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Premium – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium at St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
At St Robert Southwell, we have high aspirations and ambitions for every child. We believe that no child should be left behind. Success should not be determined by background or circumstance, but by a child’s passion for learning, determination, and commitment. It is our responsibility to ensure that all children are given the best possible opportunities to reach their full potential.
Pupil Premium funding plays a vital role in helping us to overcome barriers to learning that disadvantaged pupils may face. These barriers might include challenges with attendance, limited access to resources, or fewer opportunities to participate in wider school life.
Pupil Premium Strategy 25 – 27
Background to Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium is a grant provided by the government for children who are currently eligible for free school meals, or who have been eligible at any point in the last six years. It is designed to ensure that disadvantaged pupils achieve outcomes that are at least in line with, and often exceed, those of their peers nationally.
The Ofsted framework requires schools to demonstrate substantial improvement in progress for disadvantaged pupils. At St Robert Southwell, we are committed to addressing any disadvantage quickly and effectively so that every child achieves the highest academic standards.
How We Use the Funding
Academic Support
Ensuring that all pupils in receipt of Pupil Premium have the teaching, resources, and interventions they need to achieve at least national expectations in reading, writing, and mathematics by the time they leave our school.
Wider Opportunities
Providing funding to enable all children to participate fully in the life of the school, including access to enrichment activities, trips, and extracurricular clubs, regardless of financial circumstance.
Wellbeing and Inclusion
Directing funds towards support for our most vulnerable pupils, enabling them to access the curriculum, build confidence, and develop the social and emotional skills they need to thrive.
Our Commitment
Ultimately, all funding — whether from Pupil Premium or the school’s main budget — is used to ensure equity of experience and outcomes for every child. Our strategy is carefully monitored by school leaders and governors, and it is reviewed annually to ensure it remains effective and impactful.
At St Robert Southwell, we are proud of the progress and success of our disadvantaged pupils, and we remain fully committed to closing any gaps and enabling every child to flourish.
Pupil Premium
Pupil premium funding is allocated to St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School for children who are either currently eligible for free school meals or have been at any point in the last six years. We use this additional funding in a number of ways, including 1-1 support, emotional support and financial assistance with residential trips, outings and clubs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
Religious Education and our School Mission
Religious Education is at the heart of our curriculum at St Robert Southwell. As a Catholic school, we recognise RE as the “core of the core curriculum” and ensure that it receives the same high expectations, careful planning and importance as other core subjects.
Religious Education helps our children live our mission to:
LOVE LEARN SERVE MAKE A DIFFERENCE
Through Scripture, Catholic teaching, prayer and reflection, children discover that faith is not simply something we learn about; it influences how we treat others, how we use our God-given gifts and how we respond to the needs of our local and global community.
In accordance with the requirements of the Catholic Church and the Diocese of Arundel & Brighton, at least 10% of curriculum teaching time is dedicated to Religious Education. The Diocesan Directives require Catholic schools to give RE no less than parity with other core subjects and to devote at least 10% of taught curriculum time to it.
To Know You More Clearly
We teach Religious Education through the Religious Education Directory – To Know You More Clearly, using the Diocese of Arundel & Brighton’s Day by Day resources to support teaching and learning.
The Diocesan Directives identify Day by Day as the primary resource which meets the requirements of the Religious Education Directory within the Diocese.
From Early Years to Year 6, children build their knowledge and understanding through six curriculum branches:
Creation and Covenant
Prophecy and Promise
Galilee to Jerusalem
To the Ends of the Earth
Dialogue and Encounter
Learning builds progressively each year so that children revisit important ideas at increasing depth and develop a secure understanding of Scripture, Catholic belief, worship and the way Catholics are called to live.
How children learn in RE
Our curriculum is organised through four Knowledge Lenses:
HEAR – learning from Scripture and the Word of GodBELIEVE – understanding Catholic beliefs and teachingsCELEBRATE – discovering how faith is expressed through prayer, liturgy and the sacramentsLIVE – understanding how Catholic faith shapes the way we live and respond to others
Children also develop three Ways of Knowing:
UNDERSTAND → DISCERN → RESPOND
UnderstandChildren learn to accurately recall, explain, connect and communicate religious knowledge.
DiscernChildren learn to think critically and theologically, consider meaning and significance, examine evidence and engage thoughtfully with different interpretations and viewpoints.
RespondChildren reflect personally and spiritually on what they have learned and consider how faith can shape their lives and the choices they make.
Progression from Early Years to Year 6
Our RE curriculum is carefully sequenced so that children’s knowledge builds year by year. Key concepts, Scripture, theological vocabulary and Catholic teaching are revisited and deepened as pupils move through the school.
Teachers use children’s prior learning to plan appropriate next steps and provide opportunities for every pupil, including pupils with SEND, to successfully access and engage with Religious Education.
We have high expectations for all children and encourage them not only to remember what they have learned but also to make connections, ask thoughtful questions and think theologically.
Dialogue and Encounter
Our children learn that the Catholic Church is part of a diverse religious and cultural world.
Through the Dialogue and Encounter branch of the Religious Education Directory, pupils learn about other Christian traditions, Judaism and other religions and worldviews. They develop knowledge, curiosity and respect while becoming confident in understanding and explaining their own Catholic faith.
Assessment in Religious Education
Assessment is an integral part of teaching and learning in RE.
Teachers assess how successfully children can:
Understand religious knowledge and make connections;Discern meaning, significance and evidence; andRespond thoughtfully to what they have encountered.
Assessment helps teachers identify what children know and understand, address misconceptions and plan the next steps in learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Behaviour – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Behaviour
Behaviour at St Robert Southwell?
At St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, we believe that good behaviour is a basic requirement for effective learning. We are proud that our pupils’ behaviour has been recognised as Outstanding by Ofsted, reflecting the calm, respectful and purposeful environment that exists across our school.
Our Behaviour Policy is rooted in our Catholic mission statement:
“God gave Himself to you; give yourself to God.”
It places Jesus Christ and the Gospel values at the heart of everything we do. Each child is a unique gift of God, called to flourish in a community built on faith, respect, love, forgiveness and reconciliation.
We have high expectations of every pupil’s conduct, both in and out of the classroom. Pupils must treat each other and staff with dignity and respect, and act appropriately in all learning environments. Teachers are consistent in their routines, ensuring calm and orderly classrooms where children can focus fully on learning.
Encouraging Positive Choices
We know that children grow best when their good choices are noticed and celebrated. Staff actively praise and reward behaviour that reflects our Gospel values.
Responding to Mistakes with Compassion
At St Robert Southwell, mistakes are seen as opportunities to learn and grow. Our “Good to be Green” system provides clear boundaries while always offering forgiveness and a fresh start:
At every stage, our goal is not to shame, but to restore relationships and rebuild trust.
We cannot accept behaviours that undermine dignity or safety. These include:
Such incidents are dealt with firmly and fairly, always upholding Gospel values of justice and compassion.
Every child begins the day on Green.
Bullying
Racism, sexism, or homophobia
Physical or verbal abuse
Intimidation, dishonesty or deliberate damage to property
Supporting Every Child
We recognise that some pupils, especially those with additional needs, may require adapted strategies. Staff work with the SENDCO, parents and external agencies where necessary to support individuals effectively. Our aim is always inclusion: every child is supported to succeed.
Working in Partnership
Positive behaviour relies on trust and strong relationships between pupils, staff and parents. We work closely with families to share successes, address concerns quickly and ensure that all children feel safe, valued and supported.
At St Robert Southwell, our Behaviour Policy is far more than a set of rules – it is a living expression of our faith and values. By promoting kindness, respect, forgiveness and responsibility, we prepare children not only to succeed academically, but to grow into compassionate, principled young people who will contribute positively to the wider world.

British Values
Faith and British Values
At St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, we place Christ at the centre of all that we do. As a Catholic school, we are committed to nurturing pupils who live out Gospel values in their daily lives while also preparing them to be active, responsible and respectful citizens of modern Britain.
The Department for Education outlines the fundamental British values as:
At St Robert Southwell, these values are lived out through the Gospel, our Mission Statement and the call to work hard, be kind. By linking British values with the values taught by Christ, we help our pupils understand their responsibilities to their community, their country and the wider world.
democracy
the rule of law
individual liberty
mutual respect
Being Part of Britain
We value and celebrate both the diverse heritages of our pupils and our shared identity as part of Britain. We mark national occasions such as Remembrance Day, the Platinum Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II, the Coronation of King Charles III, and significant historical events through assemblies, curriculum study and prayer. These moments give children a strong sense of belonging and of civic pride.
Our British Values
Democracy
Rule of Law
Individual Liberty
Mutual Respect and Tolerance
Living Out Our Mission
Through our curriculum, assemblies, RE and RSHE lessons, and wider opportunities for spiritual, moral, social and cultural development, we ensure that pupils make meaningful links between Gospel values and British values.
By the time pupils leave St Robert Southwell, they have a strong moral compass, a clear sense of right and wrong, and a deep respect for the dignity of every person. They are well-prepared to contribute positively to life in modern Britain and to live out their faith as disciples of Christ.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding
Safeguarding at SRS
At St Robert Southwell, we take the safeguarding of all children extremely seriously.
The safety and well-being of every pupil is our highest priority. We have strict procedures in place for the recruitment of staff, and all adults working with our children are vetted through the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS).
Children are taught how to keep themselves safe — both in the community and online. If you ever have concerns about the safety of a child, please speak to a trusted member of staff. Concerns relating to online behaviour can also be reported directly to the Child Exploitation and Online Protection (CEOP) Centre.
The staff and Governing Board of St Robert Southwell are fully committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of pupils, in line with Section 175 of the Education Act 2002. We are dedicated to providing a safe, caring, and stimulating environment that supports the social, moral, spiritual, and physical development of every child.
We take all reasonable measures to minimise risk of harm and ensure our children’s welfare. All staff uphold a strong culture of vigilance, supported by clear safeguarding and child protection policies. These policies underpin our daily practice and reflect the shared values of the whole school community. Copies are available on request from the school office.
Any concerns about children are dealt with promptly by our Safeguarding Team, made up of trained Designated Safeguarding Leads, in line with statutory guidance on safeguarding and the sharing of information.
Safeguarding Statement
At St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, the safety and wellbeing of every child is our highest priority. As a proud member of the Bosco Catholic Education Trust, we are committed to creating a nurturing, secure and inclusive environment where all pupils can thrive academically, socially and spiritually.
We believe that safeguarding is the responsibility of everyone in our school community. It is central to everything we do and is embedded in our values, policies and everyday practice.
Designated Safeguarding Leads
All staff receive annual safeguarding and child protection training, with additional training and updates throughout the year to ensure continued awareness and vigilance.
All staff and volunteers have a duty to report any concerns about a child’s safety or wellbeing to a Designated Safeguarding Lead immediately. Any suspicions or allegations of abuse are always taken seriously and responded to swiftly and appropriately.
We work closely with a range of external agencies, including the West Sussex Integrated Front Door (IFD) and other local support services, to ensure the best outcomes for our pupils.
If you have an urgent safeguarding concern about a child, please contact:
West Sussex Integrated Front Door (IFD):
For advice regarding safeguarding concerns involving professionals, the West Sussex Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO) can be contacted via the IFD.
What is Safeguarding?
Safeguarding is about protecting children from harm and promoting their wellbeing. This includes:
Child Protection and Staff Responsibilities
Child Protection is a key part of safeguarding and refers to actions taken to protect specific children suffering or at risk of significant harm.
Parents and Volunteers
Before starting a placement at school, all parents and volunteers must read and sign our Volunteer Agreement. This includes understanding key safeguarding expectations and responsibilities.
If you have any questions about safeguarding at St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, or if you are concerned about a child, please don’t hesitate to speak to one of our Designated Safeguarding Leads. We are here to listen and help.
Email: wschildrenservices@westsussex.gov.uk
Protecting children from abuse, neglect or exploitation
Ensuring safe and effective care
Safeguarding Statement
Parents/carers are normally our first point of contact, and if a suspicion of abuse is recorded, parents/carers will be informed at the same time that the record is made; we will support parents/carers and ensure we work in collaboration with them to protect children. Working with parents/carers to prevent abuse is our primary aim and only when that has failed or in emergency situations will a referral be made to social care. When a referral is made to social care parents will be notified beforehand, except when guidance from social care or the police does not allow this.
We cannot safeguard children alone. All children’s services agencies work in partnership with each other. There are duties and rules about information sharing but if staff, parents or carers have any concerns about a child, other parent, provider, agency or any person, they have a responsibility to report those concerns and we must record and act on them. We have a St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School safeguarding /child protection policy’ which is underpinned by the West Sussex Safeguarding Children Partnership (SCP), “Keeping Children Safe in Education document” and Safer Recruitment guidance. The policy applies to all children and young people regardless of gender, ethnicity, disability, sexuality or religion. It is a requirement that all users are informed of these policies and practice guidance and what they should do if they have concerns. The safeguarding policy is available from the school office.
What You Can Do
Parents and carers play a role in safeguarding children in their community. If you have any concerns, no matter how small, you should report them to someone who you trust will listen. The school is required to have a Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) for this purpose. Parents and children should speak to the safeguarding officer if they have any concerns about a child or staff member.
If you are worried about the safety or well-being of any child in the school, please speak to a member of staff as a matter of urgency. Our Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs) are:
What You Can Do
Their role is to take lead responsibility for child protection issues in the school, including liaison with outside agencies when necessary. Our Governing Body takes a particularly close interest in all matters relating to safeguarding. There is a nominate safeguarding governor (Mrs Eva Harrison).
You can contact the NSPCC if you are worried that any child is being abused, either via their website or by telephone (0800 028 0285). The NSPCC also has excellent advice for parents about keeping their children safe, including online.
Several of our policies are particularly relevant to safeguarding. These include:

pageCache.pageTitle: Sports & Healthy Lifestyles – St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School
pageCache.text:
Sports & Healthy Lifestyles
Physical Education and Healthy Living
At St Robert Southwell Catholic Primary School, we believe that physical education is central to a child’s growth, health, and happiness. Rooted in our mission to nurture the whole child—body, mind and spirit—our PE curriculum provides pupils with opportunities to develop fitness, confidence, teamwork and resilience while also cultivating a lifelong enjoyment of sport and physical activity.
What is the Sports Premium?
Since London 2012, the Government has provided ring-fenced, substantial primary school sport funding. This funding is jointly provided by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport, and is sent directly to Head Teachers to spend on improving the quality of sport and PE for all children.
The sport funding can only be spent on sport and PE provision in schools.
Purpose of Funding for Sports Premium
Schools have to spend the sports funding on improving provision of PE and sport, but they also have the freedom to choose how they do this.Uses for the funding include:
New or additional Change4Life sport clubs.
Paying for professional development opportunities in PE/sport.
Providing cover to release primary teachers for professional development in PE/sport.
Running sport competitions, or increasing participation in the school games.
Buying quality assured professional development modules or materials for PE/sport.
Providing places for pupils on after school sport clubs and holiday clubs.
How is the Sports Funding used at St Robert’s?
The Governors agree that the money must be used so that all children benefit regardless of sporting ability; that the most able children are given the opportunity to compete in advanced tournaments; that staff have access to training opportunities and continued professional development; swimming is subsidised in order to support all families financially. The outlined report below specifies how the funding will be allocated to ensure that all pupils have extensive opportunities to participate in sport.
How is the impact of Sports Premium Funding Reported?
Our PE Leader prepares and publishes a termly report for Governors. This keeps the LGC abreast of how money is being spent, as well as the impact of actions taken.
A Broad and Inclusive Curriculum
PE is taught as a discrete subject, with all pupils receiving two hours of timetabled PE each week. Lessons span a wide range of activities including:
In Year 3, every child takes part in swimming lessons delivered by qualified coaches, ensuring they leave primary school with essential water safety skills. Pupils also complete Bikeability training, helping them to become safe and confident cyclists.
Our approach is fully inclusive: all children are encouraged to participate, take risks, challenge themselves and celebrate both personal achievement and team success.
Gymnastics, athletics and dance
Enrichment and Competition
We are proud of our strong sporting tradition. Pupils are invited to join a variety of extra-curricular sports clubs, and many go on to represent the school at local tournaments and festivals. Through these opportunities, children learn the importance of discipline, commitment and perseverance, as well as the joy of healthy competition.
We also emphasise the values of teamwork, sportsmanship, and humility in both victory and defeat. These principles reflect our Catholic ethos, teaching pupils that success is about more than winning—it is about respect, effort and care for others.
Healthy Lifestyles
We recognise the growing national concern about childhood obesity and unhealthy lifestyles. At St Robert Southwell, we work proactively to give children both the knowledge and the habits they need to live healthily.
Through PE, science, RSHE and practical experiences, children learn:
Lunchtimes and playtimes also provide opportunities to be active, with safe spaces for both energetic play and calmer activities. Water is the only drink consumed in school, and children are encouraged to eat a hot, nutritious meal each day.
School Food Plan
We support the Government’s School Food Plan by providing free hot lunches for all children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2, and encouraging pupils across the school to choose healthy school dinners. A balanced diet, shared in community, is an important part of our care for the whole child.
Our Aims
At St Robert Southwell, we see physical education not only as a subject, but as a way of helping children live active, healthy and joy-filled lives, in body, mind and spirit.
